title: Matres Lectionis
description: Some Hebrew consonant letters also help write long vowels. This unit explains the main consonant-vowel overlap and how position helps identify it.

blocks.html: Waw, yod, and final he can function as matres lectionis. In this use, waw commonly accompanies û or ô, yod can accompany î or ê, and final he can accompany a vowel at the end of a word. A mater is not a vowel point; it is a consonant letter used as a spelling aid. If the same letter has its own vowel point or begins a syllable, it is more likely functioning as a consonant.

didYouKnow: According to OSHB/MorphHB (CC BY 4.0), the most frequent word in this unit is יוֹם (yôm), occurring 1426 times in the Westminster Leningrad Codex.
